<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>As real-time surveillance and operation optimization become critical in oil and gas operations, AI-driven modeling must combine speed, scalability, and physical fidelity. This paper presents a novel forward modeling approach that integrates Physics-Informed Neural Operators (PINOs) and Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs) to predict reservoir pressure and multiphase saturation in complex subsurface reservoirs. The framework is designed for near real-time forecasting for three-phase flow in faulted, anisotropic reservoirs, serving as a core enabler of intelligent reservoir management and decision-making under uncertainty [Raissi et al., 2019; Li et al., 2020].</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This workflow leverages NVIDIA's PhysNeMo (formerly Modulus), an advanced, high-performance physics-ML framework, to train PINO-FNO surrogate models on a synthetic reservoir model (NORNE-like structural geology) comprising over one million active cells and 60 wells (injectors and producers). The inputs include static geological properties (e.g., permeability, porosity, fault transmissibility multipliers) as well as dynamic field data (pressure, saturations, rates, and PVT properties). The underlying physics is governed by a three-phase black-oil formulation, and the composite loss function integrates data-supervised loss, PDE residuals, and physics-based constraints using automatic differentiation [Brandstetter et al., 2022; Tchelepi et al., 2021]. Model training was distributed across multiple nodes equipped with NVIDIA H100 GPUs with 80 GB memory using 50 diverse model realizations.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The surrogate models demonstrated high fidelity in replicating the complex fluid dynamics of the full-physics simulator. Applied to the reservoir model, the PINO-FNO system captured spatiotemporal pressure and saturation evolution with normalized RMSE below 3%, including near-wellbore gradients and sharp saturation fronts. Critical dynamic responses such as water breakthrough, gas migration, and pressure drawdown were accurately predicted across all wells. Blind well tests validated generalization performance on unseen configurations, with the model maintaining physical realism and accurate rate predictions [Etienam et al., 2024; Almajid and Abu-Al-Saud, 2021]. Inference times dropped to milliseconds per prediction request, enabling real-time forecasting and efficient scenario analysis while honoring geophysical heterogeneity and complexity. The forward model proved effective for field development planning, real-time production surveillance, enabled workflows that demand responsiveness and accuracy and, hence, faster turnaround time and near real-time decision making.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>By coupling PINOs and FNOs within the NVIDIA's PhysNeMO framework, we demonstrated a scalable, physics-consistent surrogate capable of real-time forward modeling in complex reservoir systems. The results validate the AI-accelerated approach potential to support closed-loop reservoir management strategies and transform field operations with high-speed, accurate forecasting. Its successful application on the synthesized reservoir model establishes a strong foundation for future field-scale deployment.</jats:p>
title: AI Accelerated Forward Modeling Using Physics Informed Neural Operators for Real-Time Reservoir Management
